derivation.algorithm: the SecurityInsight release that produced this row, e.g. '2.2.457'. Resolved by Get-SISolutionVersion (engine/asset-profiling/shared/SI-SolutionVersion.ps1), which walks UP from the engine looking for VERSION then VERSION.txt, so the per-solution SOLUTIONS/SecurityInsight/VERSION wins before the repo-root VERSION.txt -- the root file carries a compound bootstrap sync label and is the fallback only. V3-6: si-v3 and main/prod write these SAME tables and the nightly runs the released code, so without this column a profile row cannot be attributed to the code that produced it. Risk Analysis has stamped this since v2.1; the profile engines did not, which is why the contamination was invisible here and visible there.

The finer Classify labels stay in IsFirstPartyMicrosoftSpn / IsThirdPartyMultiTenantSpn / AccountEnabled -- shared cross-engine asset-type field for consistent reporting / dashboards
the SI asset subtype from the ONE classification (#562): Member, Guest, Application, Managed identity; General when no row names it

fields.name: cmdbId
fields.sourcePath: cmdb.id (CMDB row primary key when matched at Reconcile)

derivation.algorithm: AUDIT #58.3 -- which CMDB source populated the cmdb* columns on this row: servicenow / generic-csv / none. Exactly one source is ever active and sources are never merged (#58.1), so this answers 'where did this cmdbCriticality come from?' from the export alone, without log archaeology.

Where this row's cmdbName came from: 'rule:<RuleId>' when a matched asset-profile rule set it (a rule's override wins over the CMDB record, field by field), 'cmdb' when the CMDB record set it, empty when there is no value. Answers 'why does this asset carry this value?' from the export alone.

Where this row's cmdbCriticality came from: 'rule:<RuleId>' when a matched asset-profile rule set it (a rule's override wins over the CMDB record, field by field), 'cmdb' when the CMDB record set it, empty when there is no value. Answers 'why does this asset carry this value?' from the export alone.

Where this row's cmdbDataSensitivity came from: 'rule:<RuleId>' when a matched asset-profile rule set it (a rule's override wins over the CMDB record, field by field), 'cmdb' when the CMDB record set it, empty when there is no value. Answers 'why does this asset carry this value?' from the export alone.
Reconcile-stage classification of how the asset was matched to CMDB: rule / identity / orphan / stale-cache / gap-cis
Reconcile-stage match outcome: matched / unmatched / ambiguous

Reconcile-stage identifier of the rule or relationship that produced the match: a rule id, 'rule-cmdbid', 'identity-match' or 'no-match'. Answers 'why did this asset map there' from the export alone. #59.3/N8 -- EMITTED since 2.3.6 but declared here only in 2.2.425; until then schema-driven tooling could not see it.

Match confidence: 1.0 for an exact match, 0.0-1.0 for the fuzzy name+environment step. The only NUMERIC member of the Cmdb* family, which is why Build-*ProfileRow.ps1 handles it outside the cmdb string-coercion list. #59.3/N8 -- EMITTED since 2.3.6 but declared here only in 2.2.425.

The matched CI's last_seen value, copied verbatim from the active CMDB source. #59.3/N8 -- EMITTED since 2.3.6 but declared here only in 2.2.425. KNOWN NAMING EXCEPTION (#59.3/N1): it carries a CMDB VALUE, so the cmdb* convention would name it cmdbLastSeen, but it pre-dates that convention and renaming would break customer queries at ~30d retention with no backfill. Exempted EXPLICITLY in SI-CmdbColumnNaming.Tests.ps1 rather than tolerated silently.

derivation.algorithm: The Entra object GUID for this principal. Prefers the ExposureGraph value (eg.user.NodeProperties.rawData.accountObjectId) when present, and otherwise falls back to the object id the builder has already resolved for PrimaryEntityId -- ENTRA_SPObjectId / ENTRA_UserId, with a final parse out of the AssetId prefix form. CHANGED 2026-08-31 from source:exposureGraph, which is why it had never populated: the row builder SKIPS a non-derived field whose required source key is absent, and EG_AccountObjectId is absent on this estate -- MEASURED 0 of 765 rows. The identifier was never missing, only asked for under a name nothing writes, which is the same species as ENTRA_UserPrincipalName -> ENTRA_UPN and EG_DeviceName -> EG_Name. Found because the asset-properties add-on resolved 0 of 1,614 Entra objects against this column: a column read by nothing cannot be discovered to be empty.

The Microsoft exposure-graph node id for this asset, promoted from EntityIds[] to a flat column. v3 step 2: the value was already collected by the EG discovery module and carried into EntityIds, but never emitted -- measured live at 72% presence inside EntityIds on endpoint rows and 0% as a column, so every consumer had to unpack a dynamic to correlate. It is the cross-engine correlation key: the same physical asset carries the same node id in every engine that sees it. Azure has emitted this column since 2.3.0; this brings endpoint, identity and publicip into line.

SI's OWN asset display name, GUARANTEED NON-BLANK on every row -- the naming half of the SI_AssetId pair, and the field a report, a connector or the correlation run report should bind to. Resolved by walking this engine's provider sources in priority order (ENTRA_DisplayName > the UPN local-part from ENTRA_UPN > MDE_DeviceName > AZ_Name > EG_Name). Two rules the unprefixed AssetName never had: a candidate identical to PrimaryEntityId is SKIPPED, because an identifier is not a name; and when no source anywhere holds a name the value becomes a MARKED SYNTHETIC 'unnamed-<engine>-<first 8 of the id>' rather than a blank or a bare hash -- so an operator can see that nothing knows this asset's name, instead of reading a hash as though it were data. SI_ PREFIXED DELIBERATELY, for collision avoidance rather than decoration: AssetName is an extremely common column name, and the unprefixed one already means a different thing per engine. The unprefixed AssetName is RETAINED AS AN ALIAS of this field, so the ~870 references in the shipped report catalog and every customer query keep working unchanged; this column is the authored value and AssetName follows it. MEASURED BEFORE THIS EXISTED (2026-08-27, live workspace): endpoint AssetName was blank on 59 of 198 rows and a 40-hex MDE machine id on 78 more -- 31% usable -- while azure (770 rows) and identity (65, service principals included) were already 100%.

SI's OWN unique asset identifier, guaranteed populated on every row. Operator intent: 'assetid and assetname was a custom unique id as an identifier so we covered 100%'. Currently an alias of PrimaryEntityId, which measured 100% on every profile table. SI_ PREFIXED DELIBERATELY, for collision avoidance rather than decoration: the unprefixed AssetId is already taken and already means three different things (MDE device id on endpoint, ARM resource path on azure, Entra object id on identity), and Risk Analysis separately populates its own AssetId from whatever each report projects -- measured live as AadDeviceId for Endpoint rows and PrimaryEntityId for Identity rows. Introducing this as a new prefixed column is purely additive: nothing that reads AssetId today changes. This is the column a connector, the correlation stage and any outbound integration should bind to.
